mainTopic: Joining different items to reach a שיעור (forbidden foods and materials for טומאה), and when benefiting from הקדש counts as מעילה.
overview: This amud finishes the פרק קדשי מזבח and opens a new פרק. First, a משנה says ערלה and כלאי הכרם join together to reach a forbidden amount, while רבי שמעון disagrees. The גמרא explains that for רבי שמעון they simply do not need to join, since any amount at all brings מלקות. A second משנה teaches that a garment, a sack, a hide and a mat join together for טומאה, because each can become טמא as a seat (מושב). A ברייתא adds that a cloth sewn from these pieces becomes טמא at different sizes depending on whether it is made for lying, sitting or holding. After the הדרן, a new משנה brings a מחלוקת about מעילה: רבי עקיבא says benefit alone is enough, while the חכמים require damage for items that wear out from use. רבא explains that they really argue only about a middle garment and fine cloth. Finally, a ברייתא begins explaining the פסוק of מעילה: it applies to everyone, and the word מעל means a change. The second proof for that meaning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Do ערלה and כלאי הכרם join together?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that ערלה and כלאי הכרם combine to make up a forbidden amount. רבי שמעון disagrees and says they do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: ערלה and כלאי הכרם join together with each other. רבי שמעון says: they do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings two different forbidden foods and says they can be added together to reach the required amount. רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה and כלאי הכרם are separate prohibitions, but both are forbidden to eat and to benefit from. The תנא קמא lets a small piece of each count together toward one שיעור. רבי שמעון says each one stays on its own and they do not combine.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree during its first three years, which is forbidden
Grain or vegetables planted together with grapevines, which are forbidden
They join together to reach the required amount (צירוף)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Orla and diverse kinds of the vineyard
join together with each other.
Rabbi Shimon says: They do not join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעׇרְלָה וְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, ערלה and כלאי הכרם combine to reach a שיעור. According to רבי שמעון, they do not combine.

steps.title: Why would רבי שמעון need them to join at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's position from a ברייתא in which he holds that even the smallest amount of a forbidden food brings מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does רבי שמעון even need things to join together? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: any amount at all is enough for lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the way the משנה presents רבי שמעון. If any amount at all already gets מלקות, there is no reason to talk about joining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joining only matters when you are short of the minimum amount and need help to reach it. רבי שמעון holds there is no minimum amount for lashes, so the whole question of joining seems irrelevant to him. Saying "they do not join" makes it sound as though he does require a minimum amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even the smallest
Lashes (מלקות), the punishment for eating forbidden food
The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And does Rabbi Shimon need them to join together?
But isn't it taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon says:
Any amount at all is enough for lashes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the משנה words רבי שמעון's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה that ערלה and כלאי הכרם do not join.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even the smallest amount brings מלקות, joining toward a minimum amount is not relevant. So the wording "they do not join" contradicts רבי שמעון's own view in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: they do not need to join
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adjusts the משנה's wording. רבי שמעון means that they do not need to join, because any amount already counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it this way: they do not need to join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rewording רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not mean that the two foods refuse to combine. He means that combining is unnecessary, since each tiny amount is already enough for מלקות. After this fix, the משנה and the ברייתא no longer contradict each other.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון holds that any amount (כל שהוא) of a forbidden food brings מלקות. So for him, צירוף is unnecessary, not forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי שמעון's "they do not join" as a leniency. He is actually the more stringent opinion here, since every tiny amount already brings מלקות on its own.

phrases.english: Teach: They do not need to join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by correcting the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון rejects joining, which would suggest that he requires a minimum amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון says joining is unnecessary, since any amount at all brings מלקות.

steps.title: Garment, sack, hide and mat all join together
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that pieces of different materials (garment, sack, hide, mat) combine to reach the minimum size needed to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The garment and the sack, the sack and the hide, the hide and the mat all join together with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case about טומאה. Pieces of different materials can be added together to reach the required size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each material has its own minimum size: a garment is 3x3 handbreadths, a sack 4x4, a hide 5x5 and a mat 6x6. Even though their sizes differ, pieces that are joined together still count toward one שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: Sackcloth, usually made of goat hair
A woven mat made of reeds or straw

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The garment and the sack, the sack and the hide,
the hide and the mat –
all of them join together with each other.
phrases.notes: They join to reach the size needed to become טמא, even though each material has a different minimum size.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבֶּגֶד וְהַשַּׂק הַשַּׂק וְהָעוֹר הָעוֹר וְהַמַּפָּץ כּוּלָּן מִצְטָרְפִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different materials combine toward the minimum size needed for טומאה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reason: they can all become טמא as a seat
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that the materials join because each one can become טמא as a seat (מושב).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: What is the reason? Because they are all fit to become טמא as a seat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the reason behind the previous ruling. The materials join because they share one form of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טומאת מושב, all these materials have the same status, since each can be used to patch a saddle or a seat. Because they have this common ground, they are treated as one kind and can be counted together.

keyTerms.meaning: A seat, which becomes טמא when a זב sits on it

steps.whatToRemember: Different materials can join for טומאה because they share the common status of מושב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason?
Because they are fit
to become ritually impure as a seat.
phrases.notes: He means the טומאה of something a זב sits on. Each of these materials can be used to patch a seat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the ruling in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The materials join because each of them can become טמא as a מושב.

steps.title: A sewn-together cloth: size depends on its use
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a cloth made from pieces of the different materials becomes טמא at three טפחים if made for lying, one טפח if made for sitting, and any size if made for holding.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if someone cut pieces from all of these materials and made a garment from them, then for lying on it the size is three טפחים, for sitting on it one טפח, and for holding it any size at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds to the משנה. It shows that the size needed to become טמא depends on what the cloth is made for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that different materials join together. This ברייתא adds that, once they are sewn into one garment, its intended use sets the minimum size. A cloth for lying on needs three טפחים, one for sitting needs one טפח, and a cloth for holding counts even if it is tiny.

keyTerms.meaning: any amount at all, even the tiniest

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
If he cut from all of them three,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the materials from the משנה: garment, sack, hide and mat. 'Three' refers to the three-טפחים measure.

phrases.english: and made a garment from them,
for lying on: three [טפחים],
for sitting on: one handbreadth,
for holding: any size at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא to the משנה's rule that the materials combine, setting sizes by intended use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A combined garment's minimum size for טומאה depends on its use: lying = 3 טפחים, sitting = 1 טפח, holding = any size.

steps.title: Why does a cloth for holding count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'for holding' means and why such a small cloth counts as a garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'for holding' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the last case of the ברייתא. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying and sitting are clear uses of a cloth. But what use does a tiny cloth 'for holding' have that would make it count as a real garment at any size?

phrases.english: What is 'for holding'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the third case in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical use makes a tiny cloth 'for holding' count as a garment.

steps.title: It protects a weaver's hands
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש in the name of רבי ינאי explains that the cloth is meant to be used while weaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי ינאי: because it is meant for weaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: even a small cloth has a real use, protecting the hands of a weaver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a tiny piece has a real, ongoing use, it counts as a useful item. That is why it can become טמא at any size.

keyTerms.meaning: for weaving (a weaving tool or task)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said that Rabbi Yannai said:
Because it stands to be used for weaving.
phrases.notes: The weaver wraps it around his fingers so the threads don't cut them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A small cloth is useful as a hand protector in weaving.

steps.title: It is useful for fig cutters
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a different use: fig cutters can use such a cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: since it is fit for those who cut figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second explanation from a ברייתא for why a small cloth for holding counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same as before, a tiny cloth has a real use, but the example is different. Fig cutters can put it on their hands so they don't get dirty.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: In a ברייתא it was taught:
Since it is fit for those who cut figs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cloth is fit for fig cutters to protect their hands.
steps.whatToRemember: A garment's minimum size depends on its use. Even a tiny cloth counts if it has a real use, like protecting the hands of a weaver or a fig cutter.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing קדשי מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק קדשי מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, קדשי מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the traditional way to close a פרק, showing we plan to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you (said at the end of a פרק)

phrases.english: We will return to you,
[Chapter] 'Offerings of the Altar'

steps.title: Benefit versus damage in מעילה
steps.stepSummary: New פרק: רבי עקיבא says benefiting a פרוטה's worth from הקדש is מעילה even without damage. The חכמים say an item that can be damaged needs damage, and an item that cannot be damaged needs only benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who benefits a פרוטה's worth from הקדש, even though he did not damage it, has committed מעילה, says רבי עקיבא. The חכמים say: anything that can be damaged, he has not committed מעילה until he damages it. Something that cannot be damaged, once he benefits, he has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new פרק with a מחלוקת. The question is when using הקדש makes someone guilty of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, benefit alone is enough. The חכמים split it: for an item that wears out from use, you need a פרוטה of damage. For an item that does not wear out, benefit alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: property that belongs to the בית המקדש
worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin value

steps.confusionAlert: Even the חכמים agree that benefit alone is מעילה for an item that cannot be damaged. They only require damage for items that wear out from use.

phrases.english: One who benefits a peruta's worth from consecrated property,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא פָּגַם – מָעַל,
phrases.english: even though he did not damage it, has misused it,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Sages say:
Any item that can be damaged,
he has not misused it until he damages it.
And an item that cannot be damaged,
once he benefits from it, he has misused it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: benefit of a פרוטה is מעילה even without damage. חכמים: an item that can be damaged needs a פרוטה of damage; an item that cannot be damaged needs only benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the new פרק: is מעילה about the benefit the person gets, or about the loss to הקדש?

steps.title: Examples: jewelry and gold cups versus clothing and axes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה illustrates the חכמים's rule. Jewelry and a gold cup are not damaged by use, so benefit alone is מעילה. A shirt, a cloak and an axe are damaged by use, so there is no מעילה until they are damaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If a woman put on a הקדש necklace or ring, or someone drank from a הקדש gold cup, once he benefited he committed מעילה. If he wore a shirt, covered himself with a cloak, or chopped with an axe, he has not committed מעילה until he damages it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives real-life examples of the two groups the חכמים described: things that cannot be damaged by use and things that can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gold jewelry and a gold cup do not wear out when you use them, so the benefit itself is the מעילה. Clothing and a tool wear down a little each time, so the חכמים require a פרוטה's worth of damage before there is מעילה.

phrases.english: How so?
If a woman put a necklace of הקדש around her neck,
or a ring on her hand,
or someone drank from a gold cup,
once he benefited, he committed misuse.
If he wore a shirt,
covered himself with a cloak,
or chopped wood with an axe,
he has not committed misuse until he damages it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives concrete examples of the חכמים's two categories from Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jewelry and a gold cup: benefit alone is מעילה. Clothing and tools: there is no מעילה until there is damage.

steps.title: Benefit from a live versus a dead sin offering
steps.stepSummary: Someone who benefits from a live חטאת has no מעילה until he damages it. Once it is dead, benefit alone is מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who benefits from a חטאת while it is alive has not committed מעילה until he damages it. When it is dead, once he benefits he has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same two-group rule to a חטאת animal, and the answer depends on whether the animal is alive or dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live animal is placed in the group that needs damage. A dead one is placed in the group where benefit alone is enough. So the same animal can switch groups depending on its state.

phrases.english: One who benefits from a sin offering:
while it is alive, he has not committed misuse
until he damages it.
When it is dead, once he benefits, he has committed misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the two-group rule from Step 12 to a חטאת animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A live חטאת needs damage for מעילה. A dead חטאת needs only benefit.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה sorts things into two groups. Things that can be damaged by use need damage for מעילה. Things that cannot be damaged need only benefit. A live חטאת is in the first group and a dead one is in the second.

steps.title: A teaching: רבי עקיבא agrees about items that can be damaged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא saying that רבי עקיבא agrees with the חכמים that an item which can be damaged needs damage for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught: רבי עקיבא agrees with the חכמים about an item that can be damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to narrow רבי עקיבא's view. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא said benefit alone is always enough. This ברייתא says that for items that get damaged by use, he agrees damage is needed. That seems to erase the whole argument.

keyTerms.meaning: An item that can be damaged by use

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was taught: Rabbi Akiva agrees with the Rabbis
regarding an item that can be damaged.
phrases.notes: He agrees that for such an item there is no מעילה until there is damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that limits רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא agrees that for a damageable item, damage is required for מעילה.

steps.title: So what are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי עקיבא agrees about damageable items, the גמרא asks where he and the חכמים still disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what, then, do they disagree?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the argument between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים is about, since the ברייתא makes them sound the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides now agree that undamageable items need only benefit and damageable items need damage. So there seems to be no case left for them to argue about.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא cancels the argument in the משנה. The גמרא is about to show that a real disagreement still exists, just in a narrower set of cases.

phrases.english: About what, then, do they disagree?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה's argument in light of the ברייתא in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is left for רבי עקיבא and the חכמים to disagree about?

steps.title: רבא: they disagree about a middle garment and fine cloth
steps.stepSummary: רבא says they disagree about a middle garment and about a garment of very fine cloth (מלמלא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They disagree about a middle garment, and about fine cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא names the cases where רבי עקיבא and the חכמים still disagree: a middle layer of clothing, and a garment of very thin, fine cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An outer coat is exposed to weather and an inner garment touches sweat, so both clearly wear down, and everyone agrees damage is needed. A middle garment, or an expensive fine garment that people treat carefully, hardly wears down each time it is used. רבי עקיבא says benefit alone is enough for these, while the חכמים say damage is still needed, since they do wear down little by little.

keyTerms.meaning: A middle garment (worn between the outer and inner layers)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא and the חכמים agree at both ends. They argue only about in-between items, such as a middle garment or fine cloth, which wear down very slowly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the argument is not about the basic rule. It is only about how to classify items that wear down so little that the damage is hard to see.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They disagree about a middle garment,
phrases.notes: This is the layer between the outer coat and the garment touching the skin.

phrases.english: and about fine cloth.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is about a middle garment and a fine garment, which wear down only very slightly.

steps.title: The law of מעילה applies to everyone equally
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word נפש that an ordinary person, a נשיא, and a כהן משיח are all included in the law of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our Rabbis taught: "A soul" means anyone at all. It includes the ordinary person, the נשיא, and the anointed כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא that reads the פסוק of מעילה word by word, beginning with the word נפש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק opens with נפש ("a soul"), which is a general word. The ברייתא reads this as including every type of person: the ordinary individual, the נשיא, and the כהן משיח. All three are equally included in the law of מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The head or ruler of the people

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
"A soul" —
phrases.notes: This is the first word of the פסוק about מעילה, ויקרא 5:15.

phrases.english: includes both the ordinary individual and the נשיא,
and the anointed priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא that explains the פסוק of מעילה. It moves on from the dispute of רבי עקיבא and the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of מעילה applies to the ordinary person, the נשיא, and the כהן משיח alike.

steps.title: The word מעל means a change
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the word מעל in the פסוק means שינוי, a change from the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: "If he commits a מעל": the word מעל means nothing other than a change.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the next words of the פסוק and defines the word מעל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says מעל means שינוי, changing something from its proper place or use. When someone takes הקדש for his own use, he is changing it from what it belongs to. The next steps bring proofs for this meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Misuse or betrayal; here, defined as a change
A change or turning away from the normal way

phrases.english: "If he commits a misuse,"
misuse means nothing other than a change,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next words of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word מעל means שינוי, a change from the proper way.

steps.title: First proof: the סוטה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that מעל means change from the פסוק about a סוטה, who "commits מעל" against her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so the פסוק says: "Any man whose wife goes astray and commits a מעל against him."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to prove that the word מעל means a change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a סוטה uses the word מעל for a wife who turns away from her husband. Turning away from the proper path is a change, so the same word in the פסוק of מעילה also means change.

keyTerms.meaning: "And so it says"; introduces a supporting פסוק
A wife suspected of being unfaithful

phrases.english: And so it says:
"If any man's wife goes astray
and acts unfaithfully against him,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:12. This is the same word מעל, used for the סוטה.

steps.title: Second proof: turning to idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins a second proof from a פסוק about people who "committed מעל" against ה׳ by turning to idols. The quote continues past the end of this passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: "And they committed מעל against the God of..."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts quoting a second פסוק with the same word. This passage stops in the middle of that פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here מעל describes people who turned away from ה׳ to serve idols. This is again a change from the proper path. The second פסוק backs up the same meaning as the first.
